svg.text: Pre-eclampsia: the disease is the placenta, so the cure is delivery
Everything else buys time safely. Nothing else cures it.
Recognising it
New hypertension after 20 weeks
plus protein in the urine
Severe features: BP 160/110 or above,
headache, visual disturbance, epigastric
pain, brisk reflexes with clonus, low
platelets, rising creatinine.
The sign nurses miss
Epigastric or right upper abdominal pain
in a pregnant woman is not indigestion.
It is liver capsule stretch, and it means
imminent eclampsia or HELLP.
Check the blood pressure of every pregnant
woman who complains of heartburn.
Magnesium sulphate — the Pritchard regimen
Loading: 4 g IV slowly, plus 10 g IM — 5 g into each buttock, deep, with lignocaine
Maintenance: 5 g IM into alternate buttocks every 4 hours, continuing 24 hours after delivery or the last fit
Before every repeat dose check three things:
Knee reflexes present · Respirations at least 16 a minute · Urine output at least 100 mL in the last 4 hours
Any one absent, withhold the dose. Antidote: calcium gluconate 1 g IV over 3 minutes, kept at the bedside.
Reflexes disappear first, then breathing slows, then the heart stops. The reflex check is your early warning.
When she fits
Do not restrain her and do not force anything into her mouth. Protect her from injury, turn her on her side,
clear the airway, give oxygen, then magnesium sulphate. Control the blood pressure. Then deliver.
Magnesium sulphate stops fits; it is not an antihypertensive. Diazepam is not first line for eclampsia.
A woman can fit for the first time after delivery. Postnatal blood pressure still matters.
